subject: Embeddings throughput anomaly after model catalog sync — Acme

From: Jill Harper <jill.harper@acme.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes on embeddings since catalog update

Hi Neha,

We started seeing a noticeable jump in embeddings latency this morning right after your model catalog sync (around 10:40 PDT). Our p95 has gone from ~120ms to ~680ms and p99 is frequently over 1.2s; overall throughput is reduced and we're getting timeouts on bulk vectorization jobs. This started coincident with the catalog update your team pushed.

Quick details:
- Example request IDs: req_53a2, req_53a9 (timestamps included in attached logs)
- Affected route: POST /v1/embeddings/text-embed-001 (customer route mapped to redwood-hosted)
- Error behavior: increased tail latency and occasional 504s when batching large payloads

We need immediate mitigation — can you route us to the prior model variant or roll back the catalog change? This is affecting downstream ranking jobs for search.

I've attached logs and a short trace. Please let me know the ETA for a fix or fallback.

Thanks,
Jill Harper
Principal ML Engineer, Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme_latency_logs.zip (zip)]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 02:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Sudden p95/p99 spikes on embeddings since catalog update

Status and preliminary analysis:
- Mitigation executed: routed Acme to text-embed-001:v2 at 2027-03-01T16:12 PDT; telemetry confirms p95 returned to ~130ms within 4 minutes of the switch. No data loss.
- Root cause (preliminary): the catalog sync introduced a variant of text-embed-001 with a different quantization profile and a new attention kernel ordering. That variant increases KV cache initialization time for long-sequence batches which amplifies tail latency under large batch sizes.
- Evidence: attached diff (catalog-change-diff.patch) shows the variant flags. Trace snapshots in the attached logs show increased memcpy time and queue wait.

Next steps:
1) Full binary bisect between v2 and v3 to isolate kernel change (INF-4321) — Rishi owning.
2) Add a safety check in catalog deploy pipeline to validate tail-latency on representative batch distributions before promoting variants. (owner: jonas)
3) Short-term: block automatic promotion of new quantization profiles for embeddings until we add regression checks. (owner: marissa)

I'll draft a short postmortem and attach timelines.

Attachments: catalog-change-diff.patch

-Rishi 
Engineering Lead, Inference Optimization | Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes on embeddings since catalog update — follow-up and next steps

Hi Jill,

Following up with a concise timeline and actions:
- 2027-03-01 10:41 PDT: Model catalog sync completed (v3 promoted).
- 2027-03-01 10:42 PDT: Acme began seeing p95/p99 spikes; tickets/telemetry created.
- 2027-03-01 15:12 PDT: Customer report received (this thread).
- 2027-03-01 16:12 PDT: We routed Acme to previous stable variant (text-embed-001:v2) — latency returned to baseline within ~4 minutes.

Root cause (summary): An unintended quantization/profile change in the promoted variant increased KV cache init and memcpy costs under large-batch embeddings, amplifying tail latency. Our deploy pipeline didn't surface this regression for long-sequence workloads.

What we did:
- Immediate mitigation: route to v2 (complete)
- Engineering: binary bisect and fix to variant profiling (INF-4321)
- Platform: add pre-promotion tail-latency checks against representative batching/sequence distributions and block autopromote for embeddings until checks pass

Ask from Acme: would you like a short postmortem and the corrected deploy plan shared with your infra/security teams? We can schedule a 30-minute review this week.

Thanks for your patience — we're treating this as high priority and I'll keep you updated.

Warmly,
Neha Kapoor
